description:
We are a team of aspiring innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, working on Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.

Our goal is to integrate and visualize satellite fire detection data to uncover patterns and improve wildfire risk awareness.

We welcome passionate teammates with skills in programming, data analysis, mapping, UI/UX, environmental science, or communication
summary:
Hotspot Hunters is a satellite fire intelligence platform designed to harmonize and compare active fire detections from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments.

The project addresses a key challenge in satellite-based fire monitoring: MODIS and VIIRS observations differ in spatial resolution, acquisition timing, sensitivity, and data characteristics, making direct comparison and combined analysis difficult.

Hotspot Hunters brings these datasets into one unified platform. It collects and standardizes fire detection data, applies spatial and temporal matching techniques, and distinguishes between detections identified by both sensors and those reported by only one. This enables users to explore the similarities and differences between satellite observations through interactive maps, timelines, comparison tools, and analytical visualizations.

The platform is designed to support fire management agencies, GIS and remote-sensing specialists, environmental researchers, and policymakers by making satellite fire data easier to interpret, compare, and analyze.

Our vision: Turn fragmented satellite fire observations into clearer, more comparable, and more actionable intelligence.
details:
Hotspot Hunters is a satellite fire intelligence platform developed to address the challenge of harmonizing active fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments.

How it works:

The platform brings MODIS and VIIRS active fire data together in one unified environment. It aims to standardize the datasets and compare observations based on their geographic locations and acquisition times. Through spatial and temporal matching, the platform helps identify detections reported by both sensors, as well as those detected by MODIS or VIIRS individually. Users can explore the observations through interactive maps, timelines, comparison views, and analytical visualizations.

Benefits and intended impact:

By making satellite observations easier to compare and interpret, Hotspot Hunters can help fire management agencies, GIS specialists, environmental researchers, and policymakers gain a clearer understanding of active fire data. It supports more informed analysis, helps users recognize differences between satellite observations, and makes valuable NASA data more accessible for research and decision-making. Our intended impact is to contribute to better-informed environmental monitoring and fire assessment.

Tools and technologies:

The project is built around NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) and its MODIS and VIIRS active fire datasets. It uses a web-based platform approach, combining data processing, spatial and temporal comparison, interactive mapping, and data visualization. No dedicated hardware is required; the solution focuses on satellite data and software-based analysis.

Creativity and innovation:

The creative aspect of Hotspot Hunters is not simply displaying fire hotspots on a map. It focuses on bringing two different satellite observation systems into a comparable analytical environment. Instead of treating MODIS and VIIRS as separate data sources, the platform helps users understand where their observations agree, where they differ, and how those differences affect interpretation. This transforms fragmented observations into a more coherent view of satellite fire intelligence.

Factors considered during development:

Our team considered differences in spatial resolution, observation time, sensor characteristics, detection confidence, data consistency, and usability. We also considered the importance of presenting scientific information clearly, making the platform accessible to users with different technical backgrounds, and avoiding misleading conclusions when comparing detections from different instruments.

Our vision:

Every satellite detection carries information. Hotspot Hunters aims to connect those signals and make their story easier to understand.
